subject: Everly mid-year uplift, burst lanes and holdback — procurement timing
messages:
From: Alicia Turner <alicia@everly.health>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:34:00 -0400
Subject: Mid-year uplift ask + procurement window

Hi David / Lauren,

Quick note from our side — usage has spiked after the latest rollout and we need to increase committed capacity starting Jul 1. We have three asks: 1) an uplift to our existing committed units for the remainder of the year, 2) an option to add a short-term burst lane for seasonal traffic, and 3) clarity on co-terming with our existing Jan renewals.

Procurement is asking for a not-to-exceed price and a PO by July 15; can you give me a formal path and timeline? Also: will Redwood consider a small holdback until we confirm the exact post-launch utilization (we're projecting a 20–30% bump but want to avoid overcommitment)?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Turner
Director, Platform Engineering
Everly Health
alicia@everly.health
(415) 555-0142

P.S. happy to jump on a quick 30-min call this week if easier.

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Turner <alicia@everly.health>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 12:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mid-year uplift ask + procurement window

Alicia — thanks for the clear ask. We can definitely get you a formal path before July 15. High-level options (I attached a draft quote):

- Option A: Committed uplift (annualized to Jan co-term) — 10% uplift discount on incremental committed units, with full annual billing; immediate capacity on Jul 1.
- Option B: Burst lane + short-term uplift — reserved burst lane for 3 months at a fixed per-token premium (lower than on-demand), plus a smaller committed uplift that co-terms in Jan; this can be structured with a 60%/40% billing split to smooth cashflow.
- Option C: Holdback-safe path — we can put 30% of the uplift units into a staging bucket for 45 days; if usage stays above threshold, the staging bucket converts to committed and invoices issue; otherwise it rolls back and you receive a credit.

I'll call out the risky bits for procurement: the holdback path requires a mutual action plan and an agreed usage trigger (we suggest 75th percentile of 14-day rolling consumption). I've attached quote v2 and a one-page MAP template to speed procurement/legal reviews.

If you want, let's do a 30-min call tomorrow 9am PT to walk the procurement team through the MAP.

Attachment: redwood_uplift_quote_v2.pdf (PDF, 220KB)
Attachment: everly_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)

— David

Subject: FW: Everly uplift — need pricing signoff and recommended structure

Ben / Neha — forwarding Everly's ask (below). They want a PO by July 15 and are comfortable with a holdback if we can offer clear conversion triggers. Key asks: 1) uplift effective Jul 1, 2) optional 3-month burst lane, 3) path to co-term in Jan.

Recommendation for approval:
- Approve Option B (burst lane + partial uplift) as standard: attach 15% uplift discount on incremental committed units, burst lane priced at 1.35x on-demand.
- Add holdback conversion clause as a negotiated addendum: staging period = 45 days, conversion trigger = 75th percentile of 14-day rolling daily tokens. If conversion happens, convert staging units to committed at the uplifted price and invoice prorated from Jul 1.
- For legal/procurement speed, pricing floor = current renewal rate; do not go below 10% discount on blended committed+burst.

Ben — can you confirm margin math and whether 15% uplift discount plus 1.35x burst preserves the margin target? Neha — if we sign Option B, can finance accept the 45-day staging logic for revenue recognition?

Thanks — David

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Final path and next steps — Everly mid-year uplift + burst lane (agreed)

Alicia / Procurement — following internal review, here is the path we can commit to and the timeline: 

Agreed commercial structure:
- Partial uplift: +220K committed tokens (effective Jul 1), priced at a 15% discount on incremental committed units.
- Burst lane: 3-month optional burst lane (Jul 1–Sep 30) priced at 1.35x on-demand. Capacity reserved, pre-warm included.
- Holdback staging: 45-day staging window for up to 30% of uplift units; conversion trigger = 75th percentile of 14-day rolling consumption. If conversion occurs, staged units convert to committed as of Jul 1 and are invoiced pro rata. If not, staged units are credited back to Everly at a 100% credit to usage.
- Co-term path: the uplift (committed portion) will co-term with your Jan renewal; billing will be annualized on conversion if staging converts.

Procurement asks / timeline:
- We need a signed Mutual Action Plan and PO by July 15 to guarantee capacity and pricing. I've attached the MAP and the formal quote (redwood_uplift_quote_v2.pdf).
- Next steps: 1) Review attachments; 2) If OK, sign MAP in the DocuSign link we'll send; 3) Procurement to issue PO referencing deal EVR-4821.

If you'd like, we can run a quick 20-minute walkthrough for procurement tomorrow at 10am PT. Otherwise, please confirm and we'll start the DocuSign flow.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you scaled.

— David
